Warner Bros. might lose out on "Barbie 2."

That’s the current risk if the studio fails to reach a deal with Greta Gerwig, Ryan Gosling, and Margot Robbie by December. Talks with the team behind the first film have been ongoing for months, yet no agreement has been reached.

According to one account, David Zaslav, head of WB Discovery, rejected what he considered overly generous terms for the creators and cast—including Gosling’s reported $20 million fee plus a share of box office revenues. But studio-aligned sources suggest the delay stems instead from demands put forth by representatives for Gerwig, Gosling, and Robbie.

Without a resolution, film rights could shift to another studio. However, any new studio would then need to assemble a fresh cast and creative team.
